findings.chapter: Ch. 5 — From Workload to Model Selection (§5.3.2)
findings.evidence: PDF p.134 (book p.110): "(Llama‑2 70B is not a GQA‑8 example: it uses 64 KV heads, so its per‑token KV matches the ~2.62 MB full‑MHA form above.)" — directly contradicts PDF p.169 (book p.145, Ch. 7 §7.3): "LLaMA-2 70B, for instance, has 64 query heads but only 8 KV-heads, so per-token KV shrinks by the head ratio to KVGQA per-token = 2 × 80 × (8 × 128) × 2 B ≈0.33 MB/token".
findings.issue: Cross-chapter contradiction on a repeated model fact (KV-head count of Llama-2 70B), and the Ch. 5 version is also factually wrong: Meta's Llama-2-70B config (num_key_value_heads = 8) and the Llama 2 paper (GQA used in the 70B model) confirm 8 KV heads, giving ~0.33 MB/token at FP16 (~3.0 GB per 9.2K request), not the full-MHA ~2.62 MB/token (~24.1 GB). A reader sizing KV for Llama-2 70B from Ch. 5 would over-provision the KV cache 8× (or wrongly conclude the model cannot use the GQA constant that Ch. 7 and Table 5-2's own GQA-8 row apply to Llama-3 70B).
findings.fix_instruction: Correct Ch. 5 §5.3.2's parenthetical to agree with Ch. 7 §7.3 and the Llama-2 70B config, e.g.: '(Llama-2 70B, like Llama-3 70B, is a GQA-8 example: 8 KV heads × 128 → ~0.33 MB/token at FP16; the ~2.62 MB/token full-MHA constant is the canonical teaching geometry, not a named 70B checkpoint).' Then sweep both chapters for any other Llama-2-70B KV statements to confirm only this one instance is wrong.

findings.evidence: Per-request context/KV cost at 9.2K input — named 70B checkpoint with GQA-8: ~3.0 GB.
findings.issue: Arithmetic check: GQA-8 (8 KV heads) reduces KV by factor of 64/8 = 8 relative to full MHA (64 heads). 24.1 GB / 8 = 3.0125 GB. Rounded to ~3.0 GB. Consistent.

findings.chapter: Ch. 5 From Workload to Model Selection; Ch. 7 Memory Is the First Constraint
findings.evidence: PDF p. 134: "(Llama‑2 70B is not a GQA‑8 example: it uses 64 KV heads, so its per‑token KV matches the ~2.62 MB full‑MHA form above.)" PDF p. 169: "Real 70B-class dense models commonly use grouped-query attention (GQA): LLaMA-2 70B, for instance, has 64 query heads but only 8 KV-heads, so per-token KV shrinks by the head ratio to KVGQA per-token = 2 × nlayers × nKV-heads × dhead × B = 2 × 80 × (8 × 128) × 2 B ≈0.33 MB/token"
findings.issue: The book gives contradictory KV-head counts and derived KV/token figures for the same named model. Ch. 5 says Llama‑2 70B has 64 KV heads and therefore ~2.62 MB/token; Ch. 7 says LLaMA-2 70B has 8 KV-heads and therefore ~0.33 MB/token. This is a load-bearing KV-sizing example and cannot stand in both forms.
findings.fix_instruction: Verify the Llama‑2 70B configuration against the intended pinned first-party source, then make both chapters state the same KV-head count. Correct the wrong occurrence and recompute/relabel every derived per-token KV figure and comparison that depends on it.

findings.page: PDF p. 133; PDF p. 135; PDF p. 136
findings.chapter: Ch. 5 From Workload to Model Selection
findings.evidence: PDF p. 133: "Every per-dollar row here is a single-stream (batch-1-equivalent) per-host figure — the illustrative rows on the 50 tok/s (20 ms/token) rate, the ~199,000 row on the canonical 25 ms/token budget — and each is a floor for the per-dollar method, not the host’s batched serving rate, so no row can be lifted as the fleet’s economics" PDF p. 135: "this chapter’s ~285,000 divides one host’s 1,583 tok/s combined single-stream rate by that same ~$20/hr." PDF p. 136: "under continuous batching (prefill of one request overlapping decode of another), on a combined prefill+decode basis the same host moves 50 × (1 + 9,200/300) ≈ 1,583 tok/s ≈ 285,000 tokens/$ (one hour of host time at that rate); the single-stream floor is 9,500/7.08 ≈ 1,342 tok/s ≈ 242,000 tokens/$"
findings.issue: The ~285,000 tokens/$ figure is inconsistently classified. It is derived from overlapped prefill and decode across requests, but the surrounding notes and reconciliation also call it a single-stream / batch-1-equivalent figure. That conflates a continuous-batching illustration with the serial single-stream floors (~242,000 and ~199,000) and makes the economic comparison basis unclear.
findings.fix_instruction: State one basis for the ~285,000 row. If it is the overlapped-continuous-batching illustration, remove all 'single-stream' and 'batch-1-equivalent' labels attached to that row and distinguish it explicitly from the serial floors. If it is intended as a single-stream result, recompute it without the second request's overlapping prefill and update the table, note, and reconciliation consistently.
